I am 33 years old, I finished middle school, and I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 10 years. My family has four people — my wife works in a garment factory in town, my father is too old for heavy work but watches the field sometimes, and my child is in school. I do almost all the farming myself. We have a well, so I can irrigate, but diesel for the pump costs real money.

I grow wheat in winter and maize in summer on the same 5 mu. That is what everyone around me does. Last year my wheat gave about 1000 jin per mu, and my maize gave about 900 jin. I want to keep that this year. I cannot afford a bad harvest.

**For wheat:** I rotary till the land in October before sowing. I use improved wheat seed — about 30 jin per mu. I buy it from the seed dealer in town, about 40 yuan per mu. For fertilizer, I put down 100 jin of 15-15-15 compound per mu as base fertilizer. That is two bags, about 150 yuan. Last year I only used compound, and the wheat turned a little yellow after winter. So this year I will topdress another 50 jin of urea per mu when the wheat turns green in March. The input dealer told me urea is 46% nitrogen, so it is strong stuff. I irrigate three times with my well: once before the winter freeze, once at jointing in March, and once at grain filling in May. Each irrigation costs me about 15 yuan for diesel. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once before sowing, insecticide twice — once for aphids in spring and once for armyworm later — and fungicide once because my neighbor had powdery mildew last year and I do not want that on my field. I expect 1000 jin per mu if the weather is normal.

**For maize:** After I harvest wheat in early June, I have less than a week to plant maize. There is no time to till. I hire the seeder to plant no-till directly into the wheat stubble. I buy hybrid seed, one bag per mu, about 60 yuan. I put 80 jin of high-nitrogen compound — 28-6-6 — at sowing. That is about 130 yuan per mu. I have never topdressed maize, and I am not starting this year. The compound should be enough. I irrigate twice: once right after sowing if the soil is dry, and once when the tassels come out. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once at planting and insecticide twice for corn borer. I do not use fungicide on maize — never had a problem with it. I expect about 1000 jin per mu, maybe 900 if it is dry.

All together, I spend about 350 yuan per mu on wheat and about 280 yuan per mu on maize. That is a lot of money. But my wife brings home some cash from the factory, so we can manage. I would rather spend a bit too much on fertilizer and chemicals than risk losing yield. If the harvest fails, I lose everything. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost I accept.
